title: Rome
blurb: HBO/BBC: Caesar to Augustus through two soldiers, Vorenus and Pullo — real names lifted from the Gallic War. The gold standard for texture and dirt.

title: I, Claudius
blurb: The BBC's adaptation of Graves: Derek Jacobi, Siân Phillips's Livia, John Hurt's Caligula. Twelve episodes, no budget, all acting.

title: Gladiator
blurb: Ridley Scott's Commodus-era revenge epic. Wrong on history, right on marble and dread. Are you not entertained?

title: Gladiator II
blurb: Rhinos, sharks in the Colosseum, and Denzel Washington. Accuracy somewhere below sea level; fun comfortably above it.

title: Ben-Hur
blurb: Eleven Oscars and the chariot race. Judaea under Tiberius, filmed at a scale Rome itself would respect.

title: Spartacus
blurb: Kubrick, Kirk Douglas, and the Third Servile War. "I'm Spartacus!" did not happen; the crosses along the Via Appia did.

title: The Fall of the Roman Empire
blurb: Marcus Aurelius to Commodus with Alec Guinness and Sophia Loren on the biggest Forum set ever built. Gladiator's uncredited parent.

title: Quo Vadis
blurb: Peter Ustinov's Nero burns Rome in Technicolor. The template for every toga epic that followed.

title: Cleopatra
blurb: Taylor, Burton, Harrison; the most expensive film ever made at the time, and it nearly sank Fox. Spectacle as a business risk.

title: Julius Caesar
blurb: Shakespeare, with Brando as Antony and Gielgud as Cassius. The Ides of March, as performed.

title: Monty Python's Life of Brian
blurb: "What have the Romans ever done for us?" The most accurate depiction of provincial graffiti enforcement ever filmed.

title: Agora
blurb: Hypatia in Alexandria, 391–415: the late Empire as a city losing its library. Rachel Weisz; underrated.

title: The Eagle
blurb: Sutcliff's Eagle of the Ninth on screen: a Roman and his slave go north of Hadrian's Wall.

title: Centurion
blurb: Neil Marshall's Ninth Legion chase movie. Blood, mud, Picts.

title: Pompeii
blurb: A gladiator, a romance, and a volcano with excellent timing. The eruption is the good part.

title: The Last Legion
blurb: Romulus Augustulus escapes to Britain with Excalibur. Somehow. Included for completeness and as a warning.

title: Spartacus
blurb: Starz: blood, sand, slow motion, and — by the end — a surprising amount of Republican politics.

title: Domina
blurb: Livia Drusilla's rise from the Triumvirate to Augustus's court. The women of the Palatine, finally centred.

title: Those About to Die
blurb: Roland Emmerich, Anthony Hopkins as Vespasian, and the Flavian chariot-racing factions. Peacock's Colosseum.

title: Barbarians
blurb: Netflix's Teutoburg Forest from the Germanic side — with the Romans speaking actual Latin.

title: Britannia
blurb: Claudius's invasion of Britain as psychedelic druid fantasy. Accuracy is not the point.

title: Plebs
blurb: Three lads in ancient Rome — The Inbetweeners in tunics. Surprisingly good on daily life.

title: Asterix: The Mansions of the Gods
blurb: Caesar tries gentrification; the Gauls resist. The most accurate film ever made about Roman real-estate development.

title: Roman Empire
blurb: Netflix docudrama in three seasons — Commodus, Caesar, Caligula — narrated by Sean Bean, with talking heads between the stabbings.

title: Ancient Rome: The Rise and Fall of an Empire
blurb: BBC docudrama in six episodes: Caesar, Nero, Rebellion, Revolution, Constantine, The Fall.

title: Meet the Romans with Mary Beard
blurb: Ordinary Romans through their tombstones, graffiti and plumbing. Beard at her best.

title: Mary Beard's Ultimate Rome: Empire Without Limit
blurb: How the Empire worked, ruled and ended, across four episodes and a great deal of travel.

title: Eight Days That Made Rome
blurb: Bettany Hughes on eight turning points, from the Rubicon to Constantine.
